papers.title_en: Calibrate Once, Fly Any Team: Residual-Grounded Low-Fidelity Training for Cooperative Drone Swarms
papers.evidence: 面向协同无人机集群训练的多智能体强化学习
papers.tldr: 高保真刚体物理训练多无人机协同策略精度高，但计算昂贵，且成本随团队规模剧增、仿真坠毁率高。为此，本文提出混合保真训练方案：在JAX原生可微低保真点质量仿真器中优化单一共享去中心化策略，并用离线短校准飞行拟合每智能体bagged残差集成来校正仿真器。在4类任务、3至18架团队规模上，该方法全面优于未校正LF基线，在24种组合中22种优于从零HF策略，最大团队时性能接近HF微调且计算成本大减、避免高坠毁率。
papers.abstract_en: Training multi-agent drone-swarm policies directly in high-fidelity (HF) rigid-body physics is accurate but computationally expensive. This cost scales poorly with team size, as each additional agent multiplies contact-resolution complexity and sharply raises the in-simulation crash rate. To address this, we propose a mixed-fidelity training scheme that eliminates HF reinforcement learning entirely.   A single shared, decentralized policy is optimized inside a fully-differentiable, JAX-native low-fidelity (LF) point-mass simulator. The simulator is corrected by a small, per-agent bagged residual ensemble fit once, offline, using short calibration flights in the HF simulator. Because calibration requires only one isolated drone, the data collection budget does not compound with team size. Reference trajectories are generated by rolling out an existing LF-only policy and tracked in the HF simulator by a zero-training PD controller.   Evaluated across four cooperative drone tasks and team sizes from 3 to 18, the residual-corrected policy outperforms an uncorrected LF baseline in all combinations, and a from-scratch HF policy in 22 of 24 combinations tested. It trails an HF-finetuned policy by a margin that narrows steadily with team size. Ultimately, the proposed method achieves near-equivalent performance at the largest team sizes at a fraction of the computational cost, completely avoiding the high crash rates typical of HF training.

papers.title_en: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous UAV Exploration in Wildfire Response
papers.evidence: 多智能体深度强化学习用于无人机集群导航与监测
papers.tldr: 野火响应中无人机自主探索面临复杂环境与实时监测挑战。本文构建多智能体深度强化学习框架，训练无人机智能体在模拟野火环境中导航与监测。实验显示智能体行为随时间更稳定有效，损失收敛、奖励提升，并形成沿火边界跟踪等一致导航模式。研究凸显了DRL无人机用于自主野火监测的潜力，并表明环境结构与奖励设计会影响策略有效性。
papers.abstract_en: This study develops a deep reinforcement learning framework for training Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) agents to navigate and monitor simulated wildfire environments. Results show that agents learn increasingly stable and effective behaviors over time, as demonstrated by converging loss trends, improved reward signals, and more consistent navigation patterns such as fire-boundary tracking. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based UAV systems for autonomous wildfire monitoring and suggest that environmental structure and reward design influence policy effectiveness.

papers.title_en: A Time-to-Collision Barrier Function Approach to Collision Avoidance for Stochastic Systems
papers.authors: Benedikt Barthel Sorensen, Mitchell Black, Erfaun Noorani, Themistoklis P. Sapsis
papers.evidence: 面向追逃的 anticipatory 规避者与追捕者碰撞规避
papers.tldr: 传统避碰约束多建立在位置或速度空间，只能对几何接近作被动反应。本文提出对抗性碰撞时间（aTTC）范式，将控制屏障函数直接定义在时间域，使控制器能预判追捕者多快可形成碰撞。由于精确aTTC需积分完整动力学，作者用轻量神经网络代理，嵌入实时二次规划控制律。在二维对比和三维多智能体追逃中，该方法优于高阶距离基线，能更有效为躲避速度显著占优的追捕者争取时间。
papers.abstract_en: Collision avoidance constraints for autonomous systems are typically formulated in position or velocity space, implicitly reacting to geometric proximity. We propose an alternative paradigm based on the adversarial time-to-collision (aTTC): the minimum time in which an adversary could achieve a collision given its dynamical constraints. By defining a control barrier function (CBF) directly in the time domain, the resulting controller is inherently anticipatory. The evading agent responds not only to whether a pursuer is on a collision course, but to how quickly it could reach one. This formulation enables velocity modulation that exploits the pursuers dynamic limits as an evasive strategy, a behavior not captured by standard distance-based CBFs. Since exact aTTC computation requires integrating the full system dynamics, we employ a lightweight neural network surrogate that admits a real-time quadratic program-based control law. We validate the approach in a 2D comparative study and a 3D multi-agent pursuit-evasion scenario, where the aTTC-based CBF outperforms a higher-order distance-based baseline by more effectively buying time against superior pursuers with a significant speed advantage.
